AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#693 @ 13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

AUD-SOL-PUSH-120, agent 120. A/B/C = 0/4/2.

First full T4 review of all eighteen P2 changed files and the original #648 history; no original APPROVE reused. Prior Sol B-648-8 lease/receipt fencing and B-648-10 quiet-hours preparation-crossing cases now pass, including the previously failing round-4 token-read/handoff-write boundary and urgency/daytime controls; B-648-1 distinct-session/thread cases and B-648-6 deadlines also pass. ([Prior narrowed verdict](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648#issuecomment-5972046897), [Round-4 before proof](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37143855203), [Replayed suites](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37343796456))

### B-693-1 — destination-time dedupe loses a distinct reschedule event

**File:line:** `src/notifications/emitters/booking.emitter.ts:264-279`, together with `push-delivery.service.ts:230-232`. The dedupe key identifies kind/session/**new start time**, not the lifecycle event; returning to a previous destination collides with an earlier, already-sent reschedule. ([Emitter](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Femitters%2Fbooking.emitter.ts), [Outbox](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fpush%2Fpush-delivery.service.ts))

**Executed counterexample:** real BookingEmitter → NotificationsService → worker, same session A→B→C→B, with five-minute gaps and each prior push drained: three inbox records but only **two** provider calls. ([Independent CI](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37344206727))

**Fix rule:** use an immutable lifecycle-event identity or persisted generation for reschedule notifications, stable on replay but different on a later real transition; reminder identities can remain schedule/generation-specific. Simply adding the old time is insufficient for a repeated A→B transition after another cycle. Preserve cross-worker same-event dedupe and add the three-transition and repeated-cycle regressions.

### B-648-7 — reopened in P2: a declared twin is not necessarily a proven twin

**File:line:** `src/packages/drip-dispatcher.cron.ts:511-544`, `src/packages/purchase-fanout.service.ts:670-703`, `src/notifications/notifications.service.ts:489-499`. Both writers unconditionally mark the push row hidden even when their separately guarded inapp write throws or returns null; the sole surviving push row disappears from list/count. ([Drip writer](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fpackages%2Fdrip-dispatcher.cron.ts), [Purchase writer](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fpackages%2Fpurchase-fanout.service.ts), [Hidden-row write](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fnotifications.service.ts))

**Executed counterexample:** the **real DripDispatcherCron writer** encounters one synthetic inapp DB failure, continues as intended, writes its one push-channel row, then the real unread count is **0 instead of 1**; the independently disabled-inapp channel case also fails. ([Actual-writer CI proof](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37344206727))

**Fix rule:** only mark a twin when a successfully committed, qualifying counterpart exists; propagate the actual created-row result/identity, or enforce the counterpart atomically. Failed/suppressed inapp writes must never hide the sole stored notification. Test both writers with throw/null outcomes and the genuine two-row counterpart case; preserve list/unread predicate alignment. This continues the original sole-row-loss finding rather than renumbering it. ([Original B-648-7](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648#issuecomment-5963265503))

### B-693-2 — receipt settlement permanently loses failed token cleanup

**File:line:** `src/notifications/push/push-delivery.service.ts:673-690,713-736`. `clearToken` swallows a DB error, `handleError` reports DeviceNotRegistered anyway, and checkReceipts permanently stamps the receipt checked. ([Exact-head worker](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fpush%2Fpush-delivery.service.ts))

**Executed counterexample:** receipt says DeviceNotRegistered; the first exact-token `updateMany` rejects once, then DB access recovers: receipt sweeps return checked counts **[1,0] rather than [0,1]**, so the known-dead token remains registered and the durable receipt never retries its cleanup. ([Receipt recovery probe](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37344206727))

**Fix rule:** settle only after token cleanup succeeds or a successful exact-token CAS proves that a newer token replaced it. Leave failed cleanup durably retryable, including ticket-stage cleanup; retry cleanup, **not the already-attempted external push**. Keep the existing protection for newly registered tokens.

### B-648-9 — reopened in P2: send preparation can outlive consent

**File:line:** `src/notifications/push/push-delivery.service.ts:462-465,473-514,547`. Preferences are read before later timezone/history/token awaits; the handoff CAS fences only the outbox lease and does not revalidate recipient authorization. ([Exact-head send path](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fpush%2Fpush-delivery.service.ts))

**Executed counterexample:** an initially enabled message enters send preparation, mute commits during a seventy-second token read (still inside the 120-second lease), and the worker subsequently calls Expo **once instead of zero**; the ordinary revoke-before-drain tests pass but do not cover this interleaving. ([Delayed revocation proof](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37344206727), [Passing original deferred-work tests](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37343796456))

**Fix rule:** move/revalidate master/per-kind authorization at the external-handoff authority point after preparatory awaits, with an authoritative snapshot/version or conditional handoff that cannot admit a revocation already committed before handoff. Suppress without deleting inbox history or spending a provider attempt, and add delayed master/per-kind revocation controls. This extends the original send-time-consent finding; do not treat the earlier, narrower deferred-queue closure as blanket closure. ([Original B-648-9](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648#issuecomment-5965118899))

### C — follow-ups, not blockers for this piece

- **C-693-1:** `push-delivery.service.ts:234-254,487-496`: per-conversation collapse and per-user burst admission are check-then-write/read operations without shared per-user fencing; two replicas can both see no pending conversation, or both see seven prior sends, and independently create/send two rows. Code-derived counterexample, not an executed concurrent-DB proof. Follow-up rule: atomic conversation admission and shared burst reservations if the 8/10-minute limit is intended as a strict cross-replica invariant. ([Admission code](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fpush%2Fpush-delivery.service.ts))
- **C-693-2, outside this diff:** `notifications.service.ts:700-735,759-813` and legacy callers still bypass this outbox's quiet-copy/quiet-hours/receipt policy; drip and purchase continue calling that old path. Follow-up rule: a separately owned T4 unification preserving each caller's truthful delivered-versus-queued contract; do not claim all app notifications are protected by this PR. ([Legacy senders](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fnotifications.service.ts), [Legacy-call example](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fpackages%2Fdrip-dispatcher.cron.ts))

### Evidence and operator decisions

- Initial independent lane: **5 failed / 80 passed**; all four candidate delivery/emitter suites pass. Refined lane: **6 failed / 33 passed**, including 32 passing drip-dispatcher controls and the passing deletion-before-handoff control; six red assertions map to the four Bs above plus canonical **B-692-1** in P1. P1's privacy finding is recorded only on P1 and is not double-counted as a P2 B. ([Initial lane](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37343796456), [Refined lane](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37344206727))
- Candidate build/test, RLS floor/live, MWB/community live, audit and schema-parity checks pass at this head; **four main-only required gates have not run on the stacked P2** (CodeQL JS/TS, banned casts, SBOM, Danger), so this is not merge eligibility. ([Candidate CI](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37152425541), [P2 stack](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/693))
- Provider InvalidCredentials behavior, deadlines, durable receipts, current-zone deferral, and existing token-CAS controls pass in the candidate suites; no live Expo/device delivery is established. ([Replayed provider/policy tests](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37343796456))

No local heavy commands, PR-branch edits, merge, production access or deployment. Recommended default: fix the four Bs in P2 and B-692-1 in P1, restack, replay both lenses' probes, and require both exact-head verdicts plus all main-based gates before landing; retain FCM setup/real-device qualification before an Android delivery claim. Track Cs separately under the freeze. Nothing needed from the owner for these bounded fixes.
